target.title: [codex] Use dashboard credits for Codex cost totals
target.body:
> **Status: product/data-semantics hold. Do not merge.** Implementation, deterministic packaged UI proof, and local validation are complete. Only owner approval of the USD-equivalent estimate semantics remains.

## Owner decision requested

**Decision:** When an attached Codex dashboard reports service credits, should CodexBar show `credits ÷ 25` as a clearly labeled **USD-equivalent usage estimate**, or continue showing local token-log pricing only?

**Tradeoff:** Dashboard credits cover Exec/Desktop/CLI activity that local logs can miss and remain scoped to the selected attached account. They are usage units, not a receipt: included-plan usage, data lag, and workspace pricing context mean the converted value must not look like billed spend.

**Recommendation:** **Approve the USD-equivalent estimate form now implemented**, then land after exact-head CI is fully green. The packaged UI proof blocker is eliminated; do not restore authoritative cost wording.

## Summary

- Converts attached-dashboard `usageBreakdown` credits at 25 credits = $1 only when the selected Codex account has an attached matching dashboard.
- Carries explicit dashboard-credit provenance instead of guessing from service names.
- Marks converted values with `≈`, labels totals as estimates, and shows the conversion source; local log costs keep their existing presentation.
- Uses the current local calendar day for Today; stale or future latest-day data no longer masquerades as current usage.
- Caps the advertised history window at the dashboard's 30-day data contract.
- Preserves matching local token/request context while dashboard credits supply the USD-equivalent values.

Official conversion evidence: [Codex credits for Students](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001147-codex-credits-for-students-terms-of-service) documents 2,500 credits as equivalent to $100; the [Codex rate card](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001106-codex-rate-card) documents credits as the usage-metering unit.

## Validation

- exact pushed head: `0ea4e61b7fef3e7400f9d7536fd5edc874483c2c`
- rebased onto current `origin/main`; contributor authorship preserved; changelog credits `@avenoxai`
- deterministic fixture model test: 1 passed
- complete `make test`: 44/44 shards passed
- `make check`: passed
- `CODEXBAR_SIGNING=adhoc ./Scripts/package_app.sh debug`: passed; packaged commit metadata matched `0ea4e61b7`
- autoreview: one accepted ambient-provider side-effect finding fixed; final review clean, patch correct at 0.82 confidence

### Source-blind packaged UI proof

The freshly packaged app was launched twice with a debug-only synthetic dashboard fixture injected at the external-input seam. The fixture traverses the normal `UsageStore` → `StatusItemController` → packaged native menu model/rendering path while disabling Keychain access, browser import, network refresh, account reconciliation, notifications, and ambient provider auto-enable.

Peekaboo capture plus local OCR/pixel inspection confirmed:

- root menu: `Today` → `≈ $10.00`
- root menu: `30d cost` → `≈ $138.00`
- root menu: `Source: OpenAI Usage breakdown · 25 credits = $1`
- Cost submenu: `Est. total (Last 30 days): ≈ $138.00`
- chart span: Jun 3 through Jul 2, proving the retained 30-day window despite an older synthetic sample
- future Jul 2 point: `≈ $100.00`, while local Today remains `≈ $10.00`, proving future/latest data does not replace the local-calendar day
- second clean relaunch reproduced the same values and source line
- no Keychain, browser-data, app-data, or notification prompt appeared

No live provider probe, real account/Keychain data, private account output, consume action, or screenshot upload was used. Exact-head CI is pending; the product semantics choice above is the sole owner decision.
